title: perf: reduce per-request overhead in the request lifecycle
body:
## Summary

Cuts per-request work in the hot path, improving the "simple" benchmark (`npm run benchmark`) by roughly **+4% mean throughput** (47.5k vs 45.8k req/s on my machine, winning 10 of 11 paired alternating A/B rounds against `main`). This brings Fastify to within ~5% of a bare `node:http` server doing the same work.

Changes, guided by CPU profiles of the benchmark:

- **`lib/reply.js`** — when there are no trailers, `writePayload` calls `res.end(payload)` instead of `res.write(payload)` + `res.end(null)`. Node corks the socket inside `end(chunk)`, so headers, payload and the finishing chunk flush through the stream machinery once.
- **`lib/validation.js`** — `validate()` bails out immediately when the route has no params/body/querystring/headers schemas, skipping four `validateParam` calls per request.
- **`lib/route.js`** — with logging disabled and the default child logger factory, the null logger's `child()` returns itself, so `routeHandler` skips `createChildLogger` entirely (two object allocations and two calls per request).
- **`lib/req-id-gen-factory.js`** — `getGenReqId` reads `contextServer[kGenReqId]` directly instead of going through the `genReqId` getter, which performed the same symbol read behind an extra call.
- **`lib/logger-factory.js`** — `now()` uses `performance.now()` instead of `process.hrtime()`, which allocates a tuple on every call. Same monotonic origin; the value is only ever used for diffs.

No observable behavior changes: responses are byte-identical to `main` (verified via curl diff), and the trailers/HTTP2-chunking paths are untouched.
